source.title: Text2PDE: Latent Diffusion Models for Accessible Physics Simulation
source.authors: Anthony Zhou; Zijie Li; Michael Schneier; John R. Buchanan; Amir Barati Farimani

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports model-size and validation-loss results for latent diffusion models in PDE simulation, a setting outside language-model pretraining. It does not fit or evaluate a power law.
record.gate_note: The paper reports PDE-model parameter counts and validation relative L2 losses for several model sizes. These results bear on scaling in another modality, but the paper does not fit power laws or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Results it cites about other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares two or three discrete sizes of PDE latent-diffusion models per dataset. It fits no power law, varies no data or compute, and changes hidden size and depth together. Loss falls with size, but two or three points cannot show the power-law form that V5 names. The 'promising scaling' remark, which cites Kaplan et al., is a qualitative comment. So this is a related size-loss observation, not a test of any version. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The main conclusion is that latent diffusion models are accurate and efficient PDE simulators that generate whole trajectories, and that text is a compact, usable conditioning modality. Scaling is a secondary remark: behaviour up to about 3B parameters is called promising and likened to Peebles & Xie and Kaplan et al. The authors suggest larger datasets could enable unified surrogates.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales latent diffusion models for PDE simulation rather than language-model pretraining; it reports validation relative L2 loss, not held-out cross-entropy, and does not fit a power law or compute-optimal split.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and conditioning modality vary; text-conditioned Buoyancy-Driven Flow losses are evaluated after re-solving the ground truth.

fits_no_version.finding: In PDE latent-diffusion models, validation relative L2 error falls monotonically with model size. On Buoyancy-Driven Flow it goes 0.3459→0.3177→0.2728 from 243M to 1.55B (first-frame) and 0.4290→0.3158→0.2944 from 334M to 2.69B (text). On Cylinder Flow it goes 0.1522→0.1309 from 198M to 667M. There is no power-law fit, data are fixed (under 5000 samples), and depth and width change together.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger latent-diffusion PDE surrogates reach lower rollout error at fixed data, across roughly one order of magnitude in parameters.

record.problems: The datasets are relatively small (<5000 samples); the reported model-size comparisons are discrete and no power-law fitting or uncertainty estimates are reported. The metric is PDE validation relative L2 loss, not language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
record.rows_left_out: 3D Turbulence results are not included because the paper reports only one size for each conditioning setting there, not a within-dataset model-size sweep. Baseline solver results are also omitted because they are not size-scaling results for the study’s latent diffusion models.

untested.parts: All: no fitted law and no extrapolation.
All: no compute-optimal allocation; dataset size is fixed.
All: depth and width are not varied at a fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in PDE or video-like diffusion models. Only 2–3 sizes, with no fit and no data or compute axis.

missing.what: Smoke buoyancy validation L1 loss by size: FF 0.154/0.139/0.118, Text 0.174/0.132. A second metric for the same size sweep.
Cylinder Flow relative L2 by size under DDIM with 10–100 steps. The S>M ordering is preserved across sampler settings.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's limits_scope label is dropped. The study shows no condition where V5 fails; it simply does not test the power-law form, which counts as untested. FF and Text parameter counts differ partly because of the text encoder. The text rows on smoke buoyancy use a different evaluation target (re-solved ground truth). The 3D Turbulence results have a single size per setting and are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens or compute.
Prediction of much larger language-model runs from power laws fitted on small runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between language-model parameters and tokens.
Effects of depth, width and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study reports size-related validation-loss results for PDE models, but does not fit a power law, establish its form, or test other listed modalities or training regimes.
Downstream-task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of language-model scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices, and curve bending.
